clue.text: Wax and massage with happy ending

parts.note: to massage is to rub

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, here of happy

explanation.surface: A beauty treatment: waxing and a massage that finishes with a happy ending.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a name game: Ruby Wax is an American-born comedian well known on British TV, so the answer is the word that goes before Wax.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedian Ruby Wax supplies the link: the first name completes her surname, a crossword-style name pairing.

clue.text: Fluster conductor

definitions.meaning: to fluster someone is to unsettle or unnerve them
Sir Simon ... is a famous British orchestral conductor

explanation.surface: A nervous moment for an orchestra leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsettle is a synonym of fluster; Sir Simon, once of the Berlin Philharmonic, is the conductor.

clue.text: Carried on as a close relative almost died

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per person', so it stands for as a

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: a sister is a close relative
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone kept going like a family member who nearly passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to continue steadfastly, so the past tense matches went on or continued.

clue.text: Relatively smart red paper pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are treated as junk to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A comparison of fashions: someone in red paper trousers looks sharper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like the garment but is the anagram signal, British slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dapper means neatly turned out; the comparative form means more smartly dressed, hence relatively smart.

clue.text: Corrupt amount mature person has to pay to receive drug

indicators.note: the fare phrase takes the drug letter into itself

parts.words: amount mature person has to pay
parts.note: the adult rate is the full fare or price charged to grown-ups
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A grown-up pays a price in order to obtain narcotics: a corrupt deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The adult rate is a ticket or entry price, as opposed to a child's fare; 'to receive' puts the drug inside that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate is to debase or make impure, which is what corrupt means as a verb.

clue.text: Down and out male with pug

indicators.note: out here means out of order or out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog-owning man who is down and out, accompanied by his pug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down and out' reads as a phrase meaning destitute, but 'Down' alone is the definition and 'out' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is the soft fine covering of birds' feathers, so it is a kind of feathering.

clue.text: Tried to sell club, then regularly stalled, leading to fierce encounter

parts.note: a salesman pitches a product, trying to sell it
a bat is a club used in sport

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of stalled

explanation.surface: A failed sale of a football club stalls repeatedly and ends in a bitter fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of stalled, TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitched battle is a hard-fought, intense clash, originally a planned battle on chosen ground.

clue.text: Hero worshipper is less fat without beginning to diet

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the slimmer word goes around the letter

parts.note: leaner means having less fat

indicators.note: the beginning to a word is its first letter, here of diet

explanation.surface: An idol-worshipper becomes slimmer even without starting a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hero' is not a celebrity but the priestess of Greek myth whom Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit; 'without' means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the young man adored the priestess Hero, swimming to her each night until he drowned.

clue.text: In Turkey, one is a bit of a pervert, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a leerer, someone who ogles lecherously, is something of a pervert

explanation.surface: A traveller in Turkey hears that someone there is a bit of a pervert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Turkish monetary unit is the lira, so one of them is a single coin of Turkey's currency.

clue.text: Some bridge getting packed is approved without consideration

parts.note: a rubber is a set of games in the card game bridge
stamped means trodden or pressed down firmly, packed tight

explanation.surface: A bridge partly crammed with traffic is waved through without proper thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests a structure over a river, but it is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubber-stamp something is to authorise it automatically, with no real scrutiny.

clue.text: Score with pious type in secret rendezvous

parts.note: in rugby a try is a score
ST, short for saint, is a pious person

explanation.surface: Someone tries to seduce a churchgoer at a clandestine meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' has a slang sense of sexual conquest, apt for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a private meeting arranged by lovers, a romantic appointment.

clue.text: Band of 7 having excursion in salacious location

indicators.note: having means holding something within, so the band's name contains the outing

parts.note: S Club 7 was a British pop band, so S CLUB is the band before its 7
a trip is an excursion

explanation.surface: A seven-piece group's day out lands them somewhere seedy.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' looks like a cross-reference to 7-across, but it is the end of the pop group's name S Club 7.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue where performers undress for an audience is a risqué, lewd place to visit.

clue.text: Unlucky, pal, she's dodgy

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A warning to a friend: she's untrustworthy, you're out of luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Hapless is a direct synonym of unfortunate, from hap meaning luck.

clue.text: Pressure on back row to sort things out in advance

parts.note: P is the standard symbol for pressure in physics
the rear is the back
a range is a row or line, as of mountains

explanation.surface: Pushing the back row in a team photo to get organised beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: To prearrange is to plan or organise ahead of time, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Don't move kitchen equipment right away

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is sent off, removed from the appliance

parts.note: a freezer is a kitchen appliance

explanation.surface: An instruction not to move the fridge-freezer and to put it right away.
explanation.definitionFit: Freeze is a command to stand absolutely still, the imperative of stopping all motion.

clue.text: Before and, unusually, after official polls

indicators.note: after means the first two pieces come behind the official

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, is a sports official
ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of and appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: Instructions for an election, with things done before, during and after an official.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda, the Latin plural, are public votes on a single question, so votes of the electorate.

clue.text: Show people fully clothed in these?

definitions.text: Show people fully clothed in these?

parts.words: Show people fully clothed in these?
parts.note: suggests a display of dressed people, but means theatre folk in costume at the final practice before a show opens

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about where you can see people with all their clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show people' reads as a verb phrase, show people; it is a noun, the cast of a show, who wear full costume in these runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Final run-throughs of a play in full costume are where performers appear completely dressed.

clue.text: One small step in wise man's lifetime of out-of-this-world travel

indicators.note: in means the step is placed inside the wise man

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
a pace is one step

explanation.surface: Echoing Neil Armstrong's moon-landing words, a wise man reflects on space travel in his lifetime.
explanation.definitionFit: The era of space exploration, beginning in the late 1950s, is a period or epoch of travel beyond Earth.

clue.text: A way less travelled overseas

parts.note: in Britain B roads are minor routes, quieter than main A roads

explanation.surface: Taking the road less travelled when going to a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are graded A (major) and B (minor), so a B road is the less used way.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad means in or to foreign countries, a synonym of overseas.

clue.text: The high and low points: in context, remarkable

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words that follow, spanning the two

explanation.surface: A comment that the peaks and troughs are noteworthy when seen in context.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrema is the mathematical plural for maximum and minimum values of a function.

clue.text: Nearly fondle a northern bird

indicators.note: nearly means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: to touch is to fondle

explanation.surface: Almost stroking a bird from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The toucan is a tropical American bird famous for its huge colourful beak.

clue.text: Bishop's bottom producing low frequency sound

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
ass is American slang for the backside

explanation.surface: A rude joke about a bishop's backside making a low rumbling noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Bass refers to the deepest range of musical pitch, the lowest notes.

clue.text: Exchange handle in Homebase, say

parts.note: to trade is to exchange
a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: Swapping a door handle at a DIY store.
explanation.walkthrough: Homebase is a British chain of DIY and home stores, so it is an example of a brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: Homebase is an example of a brand under which a business trades, a commercial label.

clue.text: Finish employment at university

parts.note: employment of something is its use
up means in residence at a university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student finishes their job at college.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish a supply is to consume it entirely, exhaust it.

clue.text: Painful back for love god

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: sore means painful

explanation.surface: The god of love has an aching back.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology Eros is the deity of desire, the counterpart of Cupid.

clue.text: Occupies fruit garden, oddly abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means those letters are dropped from the fruit

parts.note: greengages are green plums

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of garden

explanation.surface: Someone takes over a fruit garden that has strangely been left deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives GRE from garden, which comes off the front of GREENGAGES.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone's attention is to occupy it, a synonym in the sense of keeping busy.

clue.text: I'm working in the outskirts of Driffield, and it's very hard

indicators.note: in means the phrase is put inside the outer letters
the outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters of Driffield

parts.note: I'm is short for I am
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: Someone toiling on the edge of Driffield, a Yorkshire market town, finds it tough going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's very hard' reads as a complaint about the work, but describes the gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamond is the hardest natural substance, ranking top of the Mohs scale of mineral hardness.
